entries.ready_note: A SceneWidget view in the SDK (bifrost_app::view::SceneWidget) renders a scene3d Scene through its camera into the app window with the CPU triangle rasteriser (raster3d: flat shading and a depth buffer; drawables tie scene nodes to primitives3d geometry and materials), redrawing only when something changed. Dragging orbits the camera, scroll() and the + and - keys zoom, and a click picks the nearest drawable by bounding sphere through SceneView and sends an action. Host tests only. Not covered: GPU rendering, per-triangle picking, clipping of triangles that cross the near plane (they are dropped), textures, a wheel event (the SDK delivers none to views yet, so scroll() is for the app to call) and importing a scene file into drawables.

entries.name: SAML
entries.note: Left open, needs an XML-DSig engine. The job is to read and validate SAML 2.0 assertions and responses (the bundle carries the OASIS assertion, protocol, metadata and xmldsig schemas). A safe version needs a strict XML reader, exclusive canonicalization, reference and digest checks, RSA signature verification against the identity provider's certificate (rustls-graviola exposes the verifier) and signature-wrapping defences. That cannot be written and trusted without being compiled and run against real provider output, which this wave forbids; the BifrOSt accounts code has no SAML path and no XML parser. Next step: a bifrost-saml crate with the reader, c14n and verifier, tested against published SAML conformance vectors.

entries.name: ScreenReader

entries.ready_note: ScreenReader is the screen reader and its Braille output. BifrOSt has a keyboard-cursor reader over the menu bar, open menus and the front window (rotors for controls, fields, lists, menu items, text and progress; press the element under the cursor), speech through the announcement queue and the AT-SPI bridge, a Braille display output and the Braille translation (bifrost_ui::braille, the braille_text service).

entries.name: ScreenReaderCore
entries.note: Screen reader core model: Reader, rotors, speech and Braille translation, all pure and tested.
entries.ready_note: The core of the screen reader: the element walk, rotors, speech strings and Braille translation are the pure, host-tested model in reader.rs (Reader, speech, page_elements), braille_out.rs and bifrost_ui::braille.

entries.name: ScreenSharing
entries.note: VNC screen sharing viewer: Screen Sharing app over the bifrost-rfb client.
entries.ready_note: ScreenSharing is the viewer app's engine and UI (connect to another computer's screen over VNC and send keys and pointer). BifrOSt has the Screen Sharing app (apps/screen-sharing) over the bifrost-rfb protocol client: RFB 3.3 to 3.8, true-colour formats, Raw and CopyRect rectangles, DesktopSize, key and pointer input. Not built: password (VNC) authentication and compressed encodings, so a server must allow no authentication and send Raw.

entries.name: ScreenSharingKit

entries.ready_note: The kit behind screen sharing sessions: connection, framebuffer view and input forwarding, which BifrOSt has in bifrost-rfb and the Screen Sharing app. The Messages and FaceTime share-sheet transport that the reference kit also serves is Apple-only and is not mirrored.

entries.name: ScreenSharingServer

entries.ready_note: The server side that lets other computers view this screen. BifrOSt runs wayvnc (packaged in runtime-packages.txt) as wayvnc.service; Settings > General > Sharing flips the Screen Sharing switch through privd, which maps screen_sharing to that unit and nothing else. The tests cover the page model and the privd service map.

entries.name: SearchAds
entries.note: Apple Search Ads advertising service; BifrOSt runs no ad network.

entries.name: SearchAssets
entries.note: n/a: downloadable Apple-served asset packs for search (ranking and understanding data fetched from Apple's asset service). Evidence: the reference index lists only Info.plist and version.plist; BifrOSt ranks locally (ui search_rank) and downloads nothing for search.

entries.name: SearchFoundation
entries.note: Spotlight search layer: query, results, ranking and local index (quicksearch, spotindex, search_rank).
entries.ready_note: SearchFoundation is the shared Spotlight search layer: query, results and ranking. BifrOSt has the search panel (quicksearch.rs), the on-device index (spotindex.rs), the app-side indexing API (sdk quicksearch.rs) and ranking (bifrost_ui::search_rank), all local.

entries.name: SearchIntrospectionKit
entries.note: n/a: Apple internal debugging tooling that introspects Spotlight queries and the search index. Evidence: the bundle holds only Info.plist, version.plist and code signature; no user-facing resources. BifrOSt exposes no equivalent debug surface.

entries.name: SearchUI
entries.note: The search card and its results are covered: quicksearch.rs draws the query field, the suggestions and the grouped rows and opens a result; spotindex.rs is the per-app Core Search index behind the Documents group; search_rank.rs ranks the matches. Providers are the shell's own sources plus every app that indexes items, which is the same split the reference makes.
entries.ready_note: Query, grouped results, ranking and opening a result are exercised by the quicksearch, spotindex and search_rank tests. Apps contribute results by sending searchable items to the shell (spotindex); a separate third-party provider process is not needed.

entries.name: SearchUICardKitProviderSupport
entries.note: Apps supply their own search result rows: they send searchable items (title, description, thumbnail, content URL) to the shell's index (spotindex.rs), and the Search panel shows them in the Documents group and opens them in the owning app. sdk/src/search_card_provider.rs adds an in-process card registry with the same matching rule for an app that wants to preview its own cards.
entries.ready_note: The provider layer is the searchable-item path: spotindex tests cover bounded per-app storage, ranking, expiry and opening; search_card_provider and searchable_entity tests cover the SDK side. The registry is not read by the shell (the shell reads the index), so it is an SDK convenience, not a second path.

entries.name: SecCodeWrapper
entries.note: The typed wrapper over code identity checks is covered: codereq.rs evaluates code requirements over an identity, code_seal.rs verifies a bundle's files against recorded digests, codesign_events.rs reports when a running process stops matching. BifrOSt does not sign code yet, so identities come from the package manifest.
entries.ready_note: Requirement evaluation, seal verification and validity events are exercised by the codereq, code_seal and codesign_events tests. Signature checking against a signing key waits for code signing itself.

entries.name: SecureChannel
entries.note: Built 2026-10-17: ui/src/secure_channel.rs, a two-way authenticated encrypted channel between peers that pinned each other's X25519 key. One ephemeral key each way; the traffic keys come from three Diffie-Hellman results plus a transcript hash through HKDF; each direction has its own ChaCha20-Poly1305 key with the message counter as nonce (replay, reorder and tamper are refused, 2^32 message cap). Not wired into the nearby transfer yet, which still uses a shared-secret MAC. Lead 2026-10-17: not ready: no transport uses the channel yet (nearby transfer still uses a shared-secret MAC).

entries.name: SecureMessaging
entries.note: End-to-end encryption for the vendor's own message service (iMessage and its business chats); BifrOSt Messages does not use that service.

entries.name: SecureMessagingAgentCore
entries.note: The agent core of the vendor's message encryption service, which exists only to keep the vendor's message service end to end encrypted.

entries.name: SecureSessionManagement
entries.note: Built 2026-10-17: ui/src/secure_session.rs, the table of open secure channels one process holds. One live session per peer (a reconnect replaces it), a limit on sessions, an age limit and an idle limit enforced on use and by a sweep, failed messages do not count as use, and a closed session wipes its keys. Authentication-session lifecycle and login/su/sudo/ssh session events were already in core (auth_session.rs, session_events.rs). Lead 2026-10-17: not ready: no transport uses the channel yet.

entries.name: SecureTransactionService
entries.note: The secure element service for the vendor's payment cards and transit passes; the payment hardware and network do not exist on BifrOSt.

entries.name: SecureVectorStore
entries.note: Built 2026-10-17: ui/src/secure_vector_store.rs keeps embedding vectors by id, answers nearest-by-cosine queries and is stored only as one AES-GCM sealed blob under a raw key from the keychain, bound to a context string so one app's store does not open as another's. The vectors themselves come from sdk/src/embedding.rs.
entries.ready_note: secure_vector_store::tests cover ranking, replacement, bad ids, dimensions and non-finite values, the sealed round trip with hidden ids, wrong key, wrong context and tampered bytes; sealed_box and embedding tests cover the container and the vectors.

entries.name: SecureVoiceTriggerAssets
entries.note: Speech model assets for the vendor's always-listening voice trigger, which runs on the vendor's audio hardware.

entries.name: SecurityTokend
entries.note: The token layer is modelled: the token watcher and session authentication state (token_watch.rs), the keys, certificates and identities a token stores (token_objects.rs), registration of cards for sign-in (token_registry.rs, token_registration.rs) and reader slots (smartcard_slot.rs). A card driver (PC/SC) feeds these models; the models hold no key material.
entries.ready_note: All five models have tests: insert and remove events, authenticated-only objects, registration persistence and login policy, slot reports. The reader transport is the driver's job and is not part of the models.

entries.name: SecurityUICore
entries.note: The security prompts are covered: the device-owner password sheet and its attempt/lock-out model (auth_sheet.rs, auth_prompt.rs), the biometric state icon (auth_view.rs), the secure text entry (secure_entry.rs) and the permission question sheet (permission_sheet.rs).
entries.ready_note: Attempt counting and lock-out, icon states, masked entry that never leaks the text, and the allow/deny permission sheet are exercised by the listed tests.

entries.name: Seeding
entries.note: Delivers the vendor's beta feature flags from its cloud seed program to enrolled devices; BifrOSt has its own update channel.

entries.name: SemanticDocumentManagement
entries.note: Documents are managed for meaning-based retrieval: an app adds, replaces and removes document vectors (sdk embedding index), searches them by cosine (and by word with search_kit), keeps the vectors sealed on disk (secure_vector_store.rs) and indexes the documents for the system search (spotindex.rs). The vectors are hashed bags of words, not a neural model, so they match shared words and not synonyms.
entries.ready_note: Insert, remove, nearest and summary are exercised by the embedding and search_kit tests; sealed storage by secure_vector_store tests; system-search indexing by spotindex tests.

entries.name: SemanticPerception
entries.note: n/a: Apple's trained image-perception model runtime. The framework carries only Info.plist and version.plist in the reference index (no UI, no XPC service); the perception models are Apple ML model packs. BifrOSt does scene understanding through visual_search providers and subject_lift with an open segmenter, tracked in their own rows.

entries.name: SensingPredict
entries.note: n/a: Apple's on-device sensing-prediction service. The reference index shows only Info.plist and version.plist for the framework, a launch agent (sensingpredictd) and its sandbox profile; it runs Apple-trained prediction models over device context signals, an Apple ML model pack with no user-visible function.

entries.name: SensingPredictDaemon
entries.note: n/a: the sensingpredictd daemon of Apple's sensing-prediction service (launch agent com.apple.sensingpredictd, sandbox profile sensingpredictd.sb in the reference index). It hosts Apple-trained prediction models; there is no user-visible function to mirror.

entries.name: SensingPredictServices
entries.note: n/a: the SensingPredictXPCService client side of Apple's sensing-prediction service (one XPC service and its sandbox profile in the reference index). It serves Apple-trained prediction models to clients; there is no user-visible function to mirror.

entries.name: SensitiveContentAnalysisML
entries.note: private framework, owner SensitiveContentAnalysis; from SDK matrix sensitive-content-analysis.json

entries.name: SensitiveContentAnalysisUI
entries.note: private framework, owner SensitiveContentAnalysis; from SDK matrix sensitive-content-analysis.json

entries.name: SensorAccess
entries.note: The sensor models (magnetometer, altimeter, motion activity, pedometer, attitude) are tested. The sensors manifest permission is recognised by the shell policy and the SDK SensorAccess gate fails closed without it.
entries.ready_note: SensorAccess: sensors permission in app_policy (Policy.sensors, holds, ENTITLEMENT_NAMES) and sdk sensors::SensorAccess with SensorKind; tests in both crates.

entries.name: SentencePieceInternal
entries.note: An internal copy of the SentencePiece tokenizer for the vendor's on-device language models; BifrOSt ships no vendor model.

entries.name: Sentry
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal monitoring framework behind the sentryd daemon (man page sentryd.8 and the logging subsystems Framework.Lifecycle and FrameworkSignposts in the reference index; no resources, no UI). It exists for Apple's own diagnostics and signposts; BifrOSt's local crash and signpost reporting is tracked in the diagnostics rows.

entries.name: ServerInformation
entries.note: Information for the macOS Server product, which the vendor withdrew in 2022; no server product exists on BifrOSt.

entries.name: ServiceDiscovery
entries.note: DNS-SD browse and advertise over multicast DNS, plus a system-wide ServiceRegistry that keeps each app's publications, renames conflicting labels ("Den (2)") and removes one owner's services when it leaves.
entries.ready_note: Browse and advertise (ServiceBrowser, ServiceAdvertiser) and the session registry (ServiceRegistry) with conflict renaming and per-owner removal; tests in service_discovery::tests. avahi is installed.

entries.name: ServicesAnalyticsCore
entries.note: The analytics event model of the vendor's services, which reports usage to the vendor's servers; BifrOSt sends no vendor telemetry.

entries.name: ServicesAnalyticsDaemon
entries.note: The background daemon that batches the vendor's service analytics and uploads them to the vendor's servers; BifrOSt sends no vendor telemetry.

entries.name: ServicesAnalyticsKit
entries.note: The client API that lets vendor apps submit service analytics events to the vendor's servers; BifrOSt sends no vendor telemetry.

entries.name: SessionAlert
entries.note: Live activities reach the person as rows in Notification Centre's widget area with a state (pending, active, stale, ended), updated by their owning app only; an ended activity leaves after its dismissal policy.
entries.ready_note: Starting, updating, ending and dismissing an activity, and the rows the shell shows for it, are exercised by the live_activity and widgets_timeline tests. A separate alert presentation (banner with sound on update) is not built.

entries.name: SessionAssertion
entries.note: Idle and system-sleep inhibitors are taken through systemd-inhibit (logind), as caffeinate and the lid inhibitor do. The SDK PowerAssertion builds the same block inhibitor for apps (hold kind, reason, app name, command or sleep).
entries.ready_note: PowerAssertion (sdk session_assertion) builds the systemd-inhibit argv for idle, sleep or both, with the reason and app name, and wraps a command or sleep infinity; tests in session_assertion::tests.

entries.name: SessionCore
entries.note: liveactivitiesd's job is covered: the life cycle registry (request, update, end, dismissal window, the person's off switch) in ui/src/live_activity.rs, served to apps by the widgets_timeline shell service and its SDK client.
entries.ready_note: Registry life cycle, owner-only updates, stale and end handling are exercised by live_activity::tests and the widgets_timeline tests in the shell and the SDK.

entries.name: SessionFoundation
entries.note: Shared types of the live-activity daemon (content, state, dismissal, errors) are the public types of ui/src/live_activity.rs, used by the shell service and the SDK; BifrOSt keeps them in one module instead of a separate foundation layer.
entries.ready_note: Internal plumbing of the live-activity function covered by live_activity::tests and the service tests.

entries.name: SessionPushNotifications
entries.note: Receives the push tokens and wake-ups of the vendor's push service for its cloud features; BifrOSt has no such push service.

entries.name: SessionSQL
entries.note: The session store of the live-activity daemon is the in-memory Registry in ui/src/live_activity.rs, owned by the shell service (process-wide store in widgets_timeline.rs). Activities are short lived (an ended one leaves within four hours) and the owning app starts them again, so BifrOSt keeps no SQL file for them.
entries.ready_note: Internal storage of the live-activity function; the Registry and the service store are covered by live_activity::tests and widgets_timeline tests. Activities do not survive a shell restart.

entries.name: SessionSyncEngine
entries.note: n/a: mirrors live activities from other Apple devices (iPhone to Mac) through the Apple account and its cloud/continuity transport. Account-bound cross-device sync is deliberately not mirrored; the reference index shows only Info.plist for this framework.

entries.name: Settings
entries.note: The Settings app is covered: a navigation stack of list pages built from data (pages.rs), persisted options and device effects for each row (settings.rs), off-thread reads for slow panes (settings_load.rs) and a search over every pane and row (settings_search.rs). Which panes exist is tracked by the pane rows of the Settings app; this row is the framework that hosts them.
entries.ready_note: Page specs, row actions, option persistence, loading and search are exercised by the four test modules.

entries.name: SettingsHost
entries.note: The shell hosts the settings pages in-process (settings.rs), and settings_load.rs reads their stored values. Built 2026-10-17: [[settings_pane]] manifest tables parsed into the app manifest (shell/settings_panes.rs, tests settings_panes::tests). Built 2026-10-17: Settings root lists each app that declares panes, its page lists the panes, and picking one sends ae.settings.openPane over the control socket (shell/settings_panes.rs, tests settings_panes::tests; the SDK handler is sdk/src/settings_panes.rs).
entries.ready_note: Settings pane registration: the manifest tables, the Settings rows and page, and the SDK open handler are tested. The Settings page is not yet drawn on Midget.

entries.name: SettingsHostUI
entries.note: The host extension point is covered: an app declares [[settings_pane]] tables in its manifest, the shell lists them in Settings and opens the pane over the app's control socket (ae.settings.openPane); the SDK installs the handler. The pages, the Wi-Fi password sheet and the confirmation alerts are in settings.rs.
entries.ready_note: Manifest parsing, listing, the open request and its handler are exercised by settings_panes tests in the shell and the SDK; page drawing and alerts by settings tests.

entries.name: SettingsServices
entries.note: SettingsSearchReindexService's job is covered: the Settings search index is built from the page specs every time Settings searches (settings_search.rs), so it cannot go stale and needs no reindex service; the pane intents (settings_intents.rs) let Search and the agent socket list and open panes.
entries.ready_note: Index building, matching by name and keyword, and the pane intent catalogue are exercised by the two test modules.

entries.name: SettingsServicesXPC
entries.note: The service protocol to Settings is the shell's own: pane-opening intents and Wi-Fi/wallpaper action intents (settings_intents.rs, settings_actions.rs) and the app pane open method over the control socket (settings_panes.rs). There is no separate XPC process.
entries.ready_note: Plumbing of the Settings services covered by the intent, action and pane tests.

entries.name: SetupAssistantFramework
entries.note: private framework, owner Intents; from SDK matrix siri-kit.json
entries.ready_note: Apps declare [[intent]] tables in manifest.toml and serve them on their control socket. Search and the Shortcuts action library list and run an installed app's shortcut intents (shell::intents::runnable_shortcuts). The assistant answers with intent cards that run only after the user confirms them, and reads answers aloud when Speak Answers is on. Voice recognition is not built: nothing turns speech into an intent request, so Siri's spoken requests are not covered.

entries.name: SetupKit
entries.note: n/a: Apple's proximity setup framework for Apple devices and accessories (HomePod, Apple TV, iPhone-assisted setup), a sibling of AccessorySetupKitCore in the reference index and localised for the Apple setup flows. It runs an Apple-only pairing protocol with no open equivalent; BifrOSt's own first-run Setup Assistant app and Bluetooth accessory picker are separate rows.

entries.name: ShareKit
entries.note: The share sheet and its destinations are covered: the picker lists installed apps that open every shared item plus Copy and Compose Post (sharing.rs), the nearby sheet adds Save to Files and Send Nearby (share/mod.rs), and the Reading List and mail/message destinations are apps that declare what they open. The SDK sends and receives shared items (share.rs).
entries.ready_note: Target selection by type, delivery of text, URLs and files with read-only grants, the sheet model and the reading list are exercised by the listed tests. Account-picture and desktop-picture destinations are the Settings pages' own actions.

entries.name: SharePointManagement
entries.note: n/a: management of Microsoft SharePoint sites in Apple's file integration (name-based). It needs a Microsoft service BifrOSt does not have.

entries.name: ShareReporting
entries.note: n/a: the sharereportingd launch agent reports sharing events (a daemon only; the reference index shows no resources and no UI for the framework). That is usage telemetry, which BifrOSt does not collect; local recipient suggestions are in recipient_recents.rs.

entries.name: ShareServicesCore
entries.note: The core of the share services (the service list and its plug-ins such as Add to Photos) is the target list of the share sheet: any installed app that declares the item types it opens is a destination, and the transfer to a nearby device is net/share.rs.
entries.ready_note: Service discovery by manifest, delivery and the nearby transfer are exercised by the sharing, SDK share and net::share tests.

entries.name: SharedWebCredentials
entries.note: n/a: shared web credential lookup through Apple's associated-domain service, which ties into Apple's Passwords. BifrOSt keeps saved logins locally (springboard/sdk/src/passwords.rs).

entries.name: Sharing
entries.note: The job of the sharing framework is covered by BifrOSt's own nearby sharing: discovery by multicast beacon, an Accept or Decline prompt, a checksummed file transfer with progress (net/share.rs, share/*), the Settings > Sharing page with the computer name and Remote Login, File Sharing and Screen Sharing switches (sharing_page.rs) and the app share picker. The proprietary AirDrop radio protocol is not mirrored; the nearby transfer is plain LAN with a shared-secret MAC (secure_channel.rs is the building block to encrypt it).
entries.ready_note: Beacons, offers, transfers, progress, the Sharing settings page and the picker are exercised by the listed tests.

entries.name: SharingCore
entries.note: The core of sharing (peers, offers, transfers and their status) is net/share.rs, with the progress rows in share/progress.rs and the shell wiring in share/glue.rs.
entries.ready_note: Internal plumbing of the nearby sharing function, covered by the net::share and progress tests.

entries.name: SharingUI
entries.note: The sharing UI is covered: the share sheet with the preview, the row of nearby devices and the actions (share/mod.rs), the incoming-file Accept or Decline prompt (share/prompt.rs) and the transfer progress card (share/progress.rs). It draws BifrOSt's own artwork, not the AirDrop artwork.
entries.ready_note: Layout, hit testing, results, prompt and progress rows are exercised by the three test modules.

entries.name: SharingXPCServices
entries.note: SharingXPCHelper lets sandboxed apps use sharing. In BifrOSt an app asks the shell through ToShell::Share and receives items as document grants (sharing.rs, sdk share.rs), so the shell is the helper and no separate XPC process exists.
entries.ready_note: Plumbing of the share function: requests, grants and the answer to the sender are exercised by the shell and SDK share tests.

entries.name: ShazamCore
entries.note: Music recognition backend of the Shazam service that ShazamKit fronts; the SDK matrix marks ShazamKit n/a, so there is no BifrOSt counterpart.

entries.name: ShazamEvents
entries.note: Event reporting for the Shazam music recognition service; no BifrOSt counterpart (SDK matrix marks ShazamKit n/a).
